text:
incident-bot: P1 alert: Multiple customer connectivity failures via VPC peering between eu-central3 and us-east2. Symptoms: intermittent DNS resolution failures, TCP resets, and prefix withdrawals seen on RR-primary. Alert ID: ALERT-2026-17695. Please acknowledge.

maya: Acked. I see 502/504 spikes for ACME and Blumo since ~11:02UTC. Can we get an immediate impacted customer list?

cs-sam: ACME, Blumo, and Fathom have filed tickets. ACME reports client-side TCP RSTs to their API frontends. I've opened DMs with their SEs and told them we are investigating.

aj: Looking at RR-primary (eu-central3-a) BGP state. Lots of withdraws from transit-peer-22. Sample: 
```
show bgp neighbors transit-peer-22 received-routes
State: Established
Withdraws: 8 in last 60s
Routes received: 1248 -> 1216
```

nina: @aj any signs this is a misbehaving neighbor or local control-plane pressure? Also ping CPU and interrupt stats.

aj: CPU spiked to ~94% at 11:02UTC. dmesg contains RCU stalls and repeated context-switch warnings. Kernel diag job kicked off at 10:58UTC per cron. Suspect diag -> resource contention -> BFD sessions flapping.

elena: Networking confirms BFD flaps on sessions between rr-primary and transit peer; up/down cadence ~8-12s. That triggers route withdrawals, causing DNS fallback and customer 5xx. Proposed mitigation: 1) divert impacted customer prefixes to rr-standby in eu-central3-b (warm standby) 2) re-advertise via backup-transit in eu-central1 3) stop the diag job on rr-primary to recover control-plane.

maya: How quick can we switch prefixes to rr-standby? Any risk of oscillation if we re-advertise from standby and then rr-primary recovers?

elena: We can set a short-lived local-preference on rr-standby for those prefixes; propagation <45s. We'll avoid withdrawing then reannouncing primary until control-plane stable to reduce oscillation.

aj: Initiating reannounce for ACME/Blumo prefixes to rr-standby now: 
```
vtysh -c "conf t" -c "router bgp 65001" -c "neighbor rr-standby activate" -c "redistribute static route-map IMPACTED" -c "end"
```

ops: Telemetry shows traffic shifting to eu-central1 backup path for ACME. TCP flows recovering, error rate for ACME down ~68% in 2 minutes.

incident-bot: Mitigation actions in progress. Owners: networking (elena), oncall (aj), customer-success (cs-sam). Severity remains P1 until stable 30m.

cs-sam: Notified ACME & Blumo about failover to standby path and that we're pausing risky diag jobs. Both acknowledged; ACME will hold client retries during verification window.

aj: After stopping diag job, rr-primary CPU dropped to ~34%. BFD flaps dropped to zero in the last 3 mins. Routing table regained most prefixes but we're keeping impacted sets pinned to rr-standby until we reach stability window.

nina: Good. Let's do a controlled readback: start with non-critical prefixes back to primary after 20m, monitor for withdraws for 10m before moving next batch. Keep ACME pinned longer.

elena: Implemented phased drain on rr-primary for non-critical ranges. ACME & Blumo remain on rr-standby; we'll re-evaluate at 30m checkpoint.

kevin-oncall: Handoff note 1: I'm taking over monitoring. TL;DR: BGP withdraws caused by BFD flaps after kernel diag job caused CPU pressure on rr-primary. Action taken: stopped diag job, reannounced impacted prefixes from rr-standby, advertised backup-transit route. Checklist for handoff: 
- watch BGP withdraw counters for rr-primary/standby (grep for Withdraws)
- ensure customers show <1% 5xx for 30m
- coordinate with infra to post-mortem diag job params and schedule revalidation during low traffic window
- escalate to SE if customer error >5% or new withdraws appear

kevin-oncall: @cs-sam please keep customer comms until I confirm 30m stability. I'll post interim updates here.

cs-sam: Will continue updates. Posting to ACME now.

incident-bot: Checkpoint scheduled 30m. Tags: vpc-peering, bgp, bfd, control-plane, customer-impact.

maya: Added runbook notes and filed a follow-up to adjust diag job I/O niceness. Will capture logs for the postmortem.

kevin-oncall: Acknowledged. Monitoring live. Will close thread after 30m stable or sooner if things degrade.
